title: Backpropagation by hand on a two-layer graph
promptMarkdown:
A network with two inputs and one logistic hidden unit:
$$z=w_1x_1+w_2x_2+b,\qquad h=\sigma(z)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-z}},\qquad \hat y=v\,h+c,\qquad L=\tfrac12(\hat y-y)^2.$$
Inputs $x_1=1$, $x_2=-1$; parameters $w_1=0.5$, $w_2=1$, $b=0.5$, $v=2$, $c=-0.5$; target $y=1.5$.

1. Draw (or list) the computational graph: nodes, edges and a topological order. Run the forward pass and give $z$, $h$, $\hat y$ and $L$.
2. Run the reverse sweep. Give every adjoint $\partial L/\partial(\cdot)$ for $\hat y$, $v$, $c$, $h$, $z$, $w_1$, $w_2$ and $b$, showing the local derivative used at each edge.
3. Take one gradient-descent step with $\eta=0.1$ and give the five updated parameters. Then recompute the loss at the new parameters and confirm it decreased.
4. Verify $\partial L/\partial w_2$ with a central finite difference ($\varepsilon=10^{-3}$). Finally, explain in two sentences why one backward sweep produced all five parameter derivatives, and how many sweeps forward-mode differentiation would need here.
hintLadder: Topological order: $z$ depends on $w_1,w_2,b,x_1,x_2$; $h$ on $z$; $\hat y$ on $v,h,c$; $L$ on $\hat y$. Evaluate in that order; $\sigma(0)=\tfrac12$.
Start the sweep at the loss: $\partial L/\partial\hat y=\hat y-y$. Each adjoint further back is (adjoint of the child) × (local derivative of the child with respect to this node).
For the logistic unit, $\sigma'(z)=h(1-h)$; you already have $h$ from the forward pass.
The update is $\theta\leftarrow\theta-\eta\,\partial L/\partial\theta$ for each parameter separately. A negative gradient makes the parameter grow.
Central difference: $\big(L(w_2+\varepsilon)-L(w_2-\varepsilon)\big)/(2\varepsilon)$ with everything else fixed. It should agree with your adjoint to about six decimal places.
